title: Beyond RAG for Cyber Threat Intelligence: A Systematic Evaluation of Graph-Based and Agentic Retrieval
authors: Dzenan Hamzic; Florian Skopik; Max Landauer; Markus Wurzenberger; Andreas Rauber
why_relevant: Compares RAG architectures in CTI domain and examines failure modes like unsafe abstention on unanswerable queries and overconfidence with missing evidence, touching on robustness/calibration aspects.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a domain-specific architectural comparison rather than a study of robustness phenomena; robustness/abstention analysis is secondary.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Quebec Insurance: From Closed-Book to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: David Beauchemin; Richard Khoury
why_relevant: Reports RAG-induced 'context distraction' causing catastrophic regressions in some models on a Quebec insurance QA benchmark, providing empirical evidence of RAG instability.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a domain-specific application/benchmark paper; robustness analysis is shallow and dataset is private.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph Validation
authors: Farzad Shami; Stefano Marchesin; Gianmaria Silvello
why_relevant: Benchmarks LLMs with RAG for KG fact validation, touching on RAG's inconsistent reliability and contextual bias issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is KG fact validation, not directly robustness/noise/conflict/adversarial issues in RAG; only tangentially relevant.

title: Agent-Fence: Mapping Security Vulnerabilities Across Deep Research Agents
authors: Sai Puppala; Ismail Hossain; Md Jahangir Alam; Yoonpyo Lee; Jay Yoo; Tanzim Ahad; Syed Bahauddin Alam; Sajedul Talukder
why_relevant: Includes retrieval poisoning as one of 14 attack classes in an agent security benchmark, touching on adversarial corruption of retrieved content.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is broader agent architecture security (tool use, delegation, denial-of-wallet), not RAG robustness specifically.

title: SynthWorlds: Controlled Parallel Worlds for Disentangling Reasoning and Knowledge in Language Models
authors: Ken Gu; Advait Bhat; Mike A Merrill; Robert West; Xin Liu; Daniel McDuff; Tim Althoff
why_relevant: Introduces parallel real/synthetic corpora to disentangle parametric knowledge from reasoning, including a retrieval-augmented evaluation that quantifies a knowledge advantage gap—tangentially related to parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge conflict and RAG evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is on isolating reasoning vs memorization rather than robustness, noise, conflict, or calibration in RAG.

title: SUNAR: Semantic Uncertainty based Neighborhood Aware Retrieval for Complex QA
authors: V Venktesh; Mandeep Rathee; Avishek Anand
why_relevant: Uses semantic uncertainty from LLM answer candidates as feedback to guide retrieval, addressing bounded-recall in complex QA. Touches on uncertainty-aware retrieval which is tangential to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on improving recall for multi-hop QA, not specifically on robustness to noise, conflict, or adversarial evidence.

title: Retrieval Feedback Memory Enhancement Large Model Retrieval Generation Method
authors: Leqian Li; Dianxi Shi; Jialu Zhou; Xinyu Wei; Mingyue Yang; Songchang Jin; Shaowu Yang
why_relevant: Proposes iterative RAG with evidence sufficiency feedback model to terminate retrieval and filter noisy passages, tangentially related to control/when-to-stop retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is multi-hop QA accuracy via memory pool, not robustness, conflict, adversaries, or calibration evaluation.

title: RegionRAG: Region-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Visual Document Understanding
authors: Yinglu Li; Zhiying Lu; Zhihang Liu; Yiwei Sun; Chuanbin Liu; Hongtao Xie
why_relevant: Addresses distraction from irrelevant visual content in multi-modal RAG by retrieving fine-grained regions instead of full documents, touching on noisy retrieval and distraction issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is on improving retrieval granularity for visual document QA, not explicitly on robustness, calibration, conflict, or adversarial settings.

title: RealFactBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Real-World Fact-Checking
authors: Shuo Yang; Yuqin Dai; Guoqing Wang; Xinran Zheng; Jinfeng Xu; Jinze Li; Zhenzhe Ying; Weiqiang Wang; Edith C. H. Ngai
why_relevant: Introduces a fact-checking benchmark with an 'Unknown Rate' metric that measures over-conservatism vs over-confidence and evaluates LLMs with web retrieval tools, touching on uncertainty handling.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on fact-checking task evaluation rather than RAG robustness under unreliable evidence; retrieval reliability, conflict, or adversarial aspects are not central.

title: Prompting Large Language Models with Partial Knowledge for Answering Questions with Unseen Entities
authors: Zhichao Yan; Jiapu Wang; Jiaoyan Chen; Yanyan Wang; Hongye Tan; Jiye Liang; Xiaoli Li; Ru Li; Jeff Z. Pan
why_relevant: Studies partially relevant retrieved knowledge and incomplete KG retrieval, touching on noisy/insufficient evidence in RAG and how to leverage parametric knowledge when retrieval fails.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on KGQA with unseen entities and 'awakening' parametric knowledge, not core robustness, conflict resolution, or calibration under unreliable evidence.

title: ProgRAG: Hallucination-Resistant Progressive Retrieval and Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
authors: Minbae Park; Hyemin Yang; Jeonghyun Kim; Kunsoo Park; Hyunjoon Kim
why_relevant: Proposes a KGQA framework with uncertainty-aware pruning to reduce retrieval and reasoning errors over knowledge graphs. Touches on uncertainty and hallucination mitigation but in the KG-RAG setting rather than general unreliable-evidence robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is multi-hop KGQA accuracy, not robustness to noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence or calibration per se.

title: LLM-based Corroborating and Refuting Evidence Retrieval for Scientific Claim Verification
authors: Siyuan Wang; James R. Foulds; Md Osman Gani; Shimei Pan
why_relevant: Proposes a RAG extension using multi-aspect interrogation and consistency-based confidence for scientific claim verification, touching on uncertainty estimation in RAG outputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Application-focused (claim verification) rather than directly studying robustness under noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence; calibration aspect is incidental.

title: LLM-Centric RAG with Multi-Granular Indexing and Confidence Constraints
authors: Xiaofan Guo; Yaxuan Luan; Yue Kang; Xiangchen Song; Jinxu Guo
why_relevant: Proposes uncertainty estimation and confidence-controlled filtering in RAG with multi-granularity indexing, touching on noise suppression and reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Paper appears low-quality with incoherent related work citations spanning unrelated topics; contributions are vague and not rigorously evaluated against robust-RAG benchmarks.

title: Interpreting and Mitigating Unwanted Uncertainty in LLMs
authors: Tiasa Singha Roy; Ayush Rajesh Jhaveri; Ilias Triantafyllopoulos
why_relevant: Studies flip-flop uncertainty behavior in LLMs using a Needle-in-a-Haystack setup, touching on calibration/consistency under re-prompting and attention head interpretability.
why_not_or_caveat: Not specifically about RAG robustness; focuses on sycophantic answer-flipping and mechanistic interpretability rather than unreliable retrieved evidence.

title: HKRAG: Holistic Knowledge Retrieval-Augmented Generation Over Visually-Rich Documents
authors: Anyang Tong; Xiang Niu; ZhiPing Liu; Chang Tian; Yanyan Wei; Zenglin Shi; Meng Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a multimodal RAG method with an uncertainty-guided agentic generator that decides how to integrate retrieved knowledge, touching lightly on calibration/control aspects.
why_not_or_caveat: Main focus is improving retrieval coverage in visually-rich documents, not robustness to noise, conflict, adversaries, or calibration per se.

title: From Retrieval to Generation: Unifying External and Parametric Knowledge for Medical Question Answering
authors: Lei Li; Xiao Zhou; Yingying Zhang; Xian Wu
why_relevant: Proposes a method that addresses noisy/incomplete retrieval and fuses parametric with retrieved knowledge in medical QA, touching on knowledge conflict mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific medical QA application focused on accuracy gains rather than systematic robustness analysis; not a primary contribution to robustness literature.

title: Fact-checking AI-generated news reports: Can LLMs catch their own lies?
authors: Jiayi Yao; Haibo Sun; Nianwen Xue
why_relevant: Observes that RAG with search results reduces non-assessments but increases incorrect ones due to irrelevant/low-quality retrieval, touching on noisy retrieval effects in fact-checking.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is fact-checking LLM-generated news, not robust RAG methodology; RAG analysis is incidental.

title: FAIR-RAG: Faithful Adaptive Iterative Refinement for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Mohammad Aghajani Asl; Majid Asgari-Bidhendi; Behrooz Minaei-Bidgoli
why_relevant: Proposes an iterative agentic RAG framework with evidence-gap assessment to reduce noise propagation and enforce faithfulness in multi-hop QA.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-hop QA accuracy rather than directly studying robustness to noise, conflict, adversaries, or calibration.

title: Dynamic Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation for Test-time Knowledge Enhancement
authors: Yuqiao Tan; Shizhu He; Huanxuan Liao; Jun Zhao; Kang Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a parametric RAG method that claims to mitigate RAG hallucination caused by parametric-vs-context knowledge conflicts via test-time parameter injection.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is efficiency and knowledge fusion, not a systematic study of robustness, conflict resolution, or calibration; conflict mitigation is a side claim.

title: DualResearch: Entropy-Gated Dual-Graph Retrieval for Answer Reconstruction
authors: Jinxin Shi; Zongsheng Cao; Runmin Ma; Yusong Hu; Jie Zhou; Xin Li; Lei Bai; Liang He; Bo Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes entropy-gated dual-graph retrieval fusion for deep-research, addressing context pollution and noisy retrieval via uncertainty-weighted aggregation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on scientific reasoning method and aggregation, not directly on robustness benchmarks, conflict, or adversarial RAG; entropy-gated fusion is tangentially related to calibration.

title: Do Language Models Update their Forecasts with New Information?
authors: Zhangdie Yuan; Zifeng Ding; Andreas Vlachos
why_relevant: Studies whether LLMs appropriately update forecasts and confidence given new information, touching on calibration and the limits of RAG-based knowledge updating.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on probabilistic forecasting belief dynamics rather than RAG robustness per se; RAG is mentioned tangentially.

title: Decoupling Reasoning and Knowledge Injection for In-Context Knowledge Editing
authors: Changyue Wang; Weihang Su; Qingyao Ai; Yujia Zhou; Yiqun Liu
why_relevant: Addresses conflict between injected contextual knowledge and LLM parametric knowledge in in-context knowledge editing, tangentially related to retrieved-vs-parametric conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on knowledge editing rather than RAG robustness; not about unreliable retrieved evidence per se.

title: Confidence-Aware Routing for Large Language Model Reliability Enhancement: A Multi-Signal Approach to Pre-Generation Hallucination Mitigation
authors: Nandakishor M
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes a pre-generation confidence routing system that decides between local generation, RAG, larger models, or human review, touching on when-to-retrieve and abstention control.
why_not_or_caveat: Evaluation is weak (72 training examples, small model), and the work is not specifically about RAG robustness under unreliable evidence; routing is generic confidence-based.

title: Auto-ARGUE: LLM-Based Report Generation Evaluation
authors: William Walden; Marc Mason; Orion Weller; Laura Dietz; John Conroy; Neil Molino; Hannah Recknor; Bryan Li; Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu; Yu Hou; Dawn Lawrie; James Mayfield; Eugene Yang
why_relevant: Auto-ARGUE evaluates citation-backed report generation in RAG, including assertions of ignorance and citation support, which touches on attribution and abstention evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on report generation evaluation broadly, not specifically on robustness to noise, conflict, adversaries, or calibration.

title: AcuRank: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Computation for Listwise Reranking
authors: Soyoung Yoon; Gyuwan Kim; Gyu-Hwung Cho; Seung-won Hwang
why_relevant: Proposes uncertainty-aware adaptive listwise reranking using Bayesian TrueSkill, relevant to retrieval quality and confidence-driven computation that could improve RAG evidence reliability.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on reranking efficiency rather than robustness of RAG under noisy/adversarial/conflicting evidence; uncertainty is over ranking, not generation.

title: A Decentralized Retrieval Augmented Generation System with Source Reliabilities Secured on Blockchain
authors: Yining Lu; Wenyi Tang; Max Johnson; Taeho Jung; Meng Jiang
why_relevant: Proposes a source reliability scoring mechanism for decentralized RAG to handle unreliable data sources with varying quality (noise, misinformation, outdated content).
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is decentralized architecture and blockchain-based trust management, not robustness methodology per se; relevance to robust RAG is tangential.

title: Towards Better Generalization in Open-Domain Question Answering by Mitigating Context Memorization
authors: Zixuan Zhang; Revanth Gangi Reddy; Kevin Small; Tong Zhang; Heng Ji
why_relevant: Addresses reader over-memorization of retrieved corpus, which relates to parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge reliance and generalization to updated/new corpora (distribution shift).
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on generalization across corpus updates/domains rather than directly on robustness to noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence.

title: QPaug: Question and Passage Augmentation for Open-Domain Question Answering of LLMs
authors: Minsang Kim; Cheoneum Park; Seungjun Baek
why_relevant: Proposes question/passage augmentation to mitigate poor retrieval quality and distracting passages in ODQA, touching on noisy retrieval issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily an ODQA performance method, not a robustness-focused study; does not systematically address noise, conflict, or calibration.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
authors: Di Wu; Hongwei Wang; Wenhao Yu; Yuwei Zhang; Kai-Wei Chang; Dong Yu
why_relevant: LongMemEval benchmarks long-term memory in chat assistants, including abstention on unanswerable questions and knowledge updates, which touch on calibration and conflict handling in retrieval-augmented memory systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary focus is memory/personalization benchmarking, not robustness of RAG under noisy, adversarial, or conflicting evidence.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
authors: Yangning Li; Yinghui Li; Xinyu Wang; Yong Jiang; Zhen Zhang; Xinran Zheng; Hui Wang; Hai-Tao Zheng; Philip S. Yu; Fei Huang; Jingren Zhou
why_relevant: Proposes a multimodal RAG benchmark with dynamic questions and an adaptive planning agent that decides when/how to retrieve, touching on adaptive retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multimodal VQA complexity and adaptive retrieval planning, not on robustness to noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence or calibration/abstention.

title: Are LLM-Based Retrievers Worth Their Cost? An Empirical Study of Efficiency, Robustness, and Reasoning Overhead
authors: Abdelrahman Abdallah; Jamie Holdcroft; Mohammed Ali; Adam Jatowt
why_relevant: Studies retriever robustness to query perturbations and confidence calibration (AUROC) for retrieval scores, touching on calibration/control aspects relevant to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retriever-side efficiency/effectiveness trade-offs rather than RAG pipeline robustness to unreliable evidence; calibration analysis is limited to raw retrieval scores.

title: Language-Coupled Reinforcement Learning for Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Rui Qi; Fengran Mo; Yufeng Chen; Xue Zhang; Shuo Wang; Hongliang Li; Jinan Xu; Meng Jiang; Jian-Yun Nie; Kaiyu Huang
why_relevant: Addresses knowledge conflict and bias in multilingual RAG via RL-based rollout and reward design, touching on conflict mitigation across retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a multilingual MRAG method paper; conflict handling is incidental to cross-lingual optimization rather than a focused robustness study.

title: Empirical Characterization of Inference-Time Elicited Probability Transformations in Large Language Models
authors: Mike Farmer; Abhinav Kochar; Yugyung Lee
why_relevant: Studies how inference-time prompting (including retrieval augmentation and verifier feedback) transforms elicited probabilities, with implications for calibration and evidence amplification.
why_not_or_caveat: Not specific to RAG robustness; focuses on general log-ratio probability transformations across prompting pipelines rather than unreliable evidence handling.
